response.report:
EXAM: Chest radiograph, one view, 2026-11-19
CLINICAL INDICATION: On treatment for metastatic colorectal cancer. Increasing shortness of breath over one week.
ORDERING PROVIDER: Dr. M. Castellanos (synthetic), medical oncology
COMPARISON: Chest radiograph, 2026-09-02
TECHNIQUE: Current PA. Prior PA. Same projection on both. Differences from prior: the prior has higher contrast and mild rotation. The current is softer and flatter, with no rotation. These differences limit comparison of subtle density change at the hila and of small nodules, and limit comparison of hilar size and mediastinal contour.

LOOK AT FIRST:
- None of these findings is flagged time-sensitive. Listed in priority order:
- F1: Left hilum, possible adenopathy. Indeterminate. Only one of two reads reported it (read A, indeterminate).
- F6: Left hilum, fullness and small ring lucency. Only one of two reads reported it (read B, stable).
- F5: Right lower zone, coarse interstitial markings. Only one of two reads reported it (read A, stable).
- F8: Right lower zone, prominent bronchovascular markings. Only one of two reads reported it (read B, stable).
- F7: Cardiac silhouette. Only one of two reads reported it (read B, stable).

FINDINGS (systematic read, done blind to the indication):
- Airway / lungs: Trachea is central with no central airway narrowing at this resolution. Lung volumes are large. No focal consolidation, collapse or discrete mass in any zone. Mildly coarse markings in the right lower zone, with no focal consolidation, similar on both studies (F5, F8; each reported by one of two reads). Overlying soft tissue may contribute to the right lower zone haze. A tiny density over the right medial upper zone is seen on the prior only (see CAN'T DETERMINE).
- Mediastinum / hila: Prominent aortic knuckle consistent with an unfolded aorta. Upper mediastinum is not widened. Similar on both studies (F4, both reads agree). Right hilum is unremarkable. Left hilum: fuller and denser on the prior than on the current, and the current left hilum is not bulky. Status is indeterminate (F1, reported by read A only), because the prior's higher contrast and mild rotation may explain the difference. Read B did not report this change and recorded the left hilum as fuller and denser than the right on both studies with similar contour and bulk (F6, stable). A small ring lucency over the left hilum on the current study is possibly an end-on bronchus. Size change for F1 is described in words only: smaller on the current, needs measurement.
- Pleura: Both costophrenic angles are sharp. No pleural line and no visible pleural thickening. Diaphragm / upper abdomen: the left dome is level with or slightly higher than the right, with gas-filled stomach and colon beneath it. Gas distension under the left dome is indeterminate for change (F3): the two reads disagreed (read A stable, read B decreased). No gas under the right dome on either study.
- Heart: Cardiac silhouette at the upper limit of normal for a PA film, with sharp borders, and similar in size and contour to the prior (F7, reported by one of two reads).
- Bones / soft tissue: No displaced rib fracture or destructive rib lesion at this resolution. Degenerative change at both shoulders and the lower cervical spine. No soft tissue gas. Fine bone detail is limited. Devices: left-sided central venous catheter with its tip projecting over the expected superior vena cava, same course and tip position on both studies, no new device (F2, both reads agree).

INTERVAL CHANGE:
- Changed: Left hilar fullness appears smaller on the current than the prior, but this is indeterminate (F1) and read B recorded the left hilum as stable (F6). Gas distension under the left dome is indeterminate for change because the reads disagreed (F3, stable vs decreased).
- Unchanged: Left-sided central venous catheter (F2). Aortic knuckle and mediastinal width (F4). Coarse right lower zone markings (F5, F8). Cardiac silhouette (F7). No new consolidation, pleural effusion, pneumothorax, or new lung nodule or mass compared with the prior.

RECIST 1.1: Not computed. No confirmed measurements.

CAN'T DETERMINE:
- Is the left hilum truly smaller on the current study than on the prior? | Reason: The prior has higher contrast and mild rotation, and both can make one hilum look larger and denser. A frontal film alone does not separate vessel from node or mass. | Recommend: CT chest with contrast, and review of the source images in PACS.
- Is the tiny density over the right medial upper zone on the prior a lung nodule or first rib costochondral calcification? | Reason: The density is well under the size at which X-ray separates a nodule from bone or a vessel end-on. It is not clearly seen on the lower-contrast current film. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS. CT chest if it persists on review.
- Is there opacity behind the heart or at the left base? | Reason: The relatively high left dome and gas-filled bowel overlap the left base and retrocardiac region on a frontal film alone. | Recommend: Lateral view or CT chest.
- Is there a focal bone lesion in the ribs, shoulders or spine? | Reason: The images are low resolution and compressed, so fine bone detail is not assessable. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS.
- Is the left hilar fullness vascular (pulmonary artery) or nodal? | Reason: A frontal film alone cannot separate vessel from lymph node, and the difference in image contrast between the two studies limits judgment of subtle density change. | Recommend: Correlate with any previous cross-sectional imaging. If none is available, contrast-enhanced CT chest.
- Is the small ring lucency over the left hilum on the current study a bronchus seen end-on or a small cavitary or cystic focus? | Reason: The structure is small, overlaps hilar vessels, and is seen on a downsampled frontal image only. It is less conspicuous on the higher-contrast prior. | Recommend: Review the source image in PACS. Lateral view or CT chest if it persists.
- Does the asymmetry of the breast shadows reflect previous left breast surgery, or positioning? | Reason: Soft-tissue contours are partly outside the field and faint at this resolution. The asymmetry makes the right lower zone look hazier than the left on both studies. | Recommend: Correlate with surgical history. Do not read the right lower zone haze as lung opacity without that correlation.
- What is the exact catheter tip position relative to the cavoatrial junction, and what type of line is it? | Reason: The carina and the right atrial junction are not sharply defined on these images, and the insertion site and any reservoir lie outside the field. | Recommend: Review the source image in PACS with windowing. Correlate with the line insertion record.
- Are there small nodules in the retrocardiac region, at the apices or behind the diaphragm domes? | Reason: Only a single frontal view of each study is available. These areas are hidden by overlap, and small nodules cannot be separated from vessels seen end-on or from rib ends. | Recommend: Lateral view, or CT chest if there is clinical concern.
- Is there a subtle rib, spine or shoulder lesion? | Reason: The images are low resolution and compressed, and fine bone detail such as cortex, pedicles and small lucent lesions is not reliably shown. | Recommend: Review the source images in PACS on bone settings.

IMPRESSION:
1. Left hilum (F1): possible adenopathy with indeterminate interval change. The left hilum appears smaller on the current, but contrast and rotation differences between studies prevent a confident call. Only read A reported this finding. Needs measurement and radiologist review.
2. Left hilum (F6): fullness similar on both studies per read B. A small ring lucency on the current is possibly an end-on bronchus and is not further characterized (see CAN'T DETERMINE). Only read B reported this finding.
3. Right lower zone (F5, F8): mildly coarse or prominent markings without focal consolidation, similar to the prior. Overlying soft tissue may contribute.
4. Heart (F7): cardiac silhouette at the upper limit of normal for a PA film and similar to the prior.
5. No new consolidation, pleural effusion, pneumothorax, or new lung nodule or mass compared with the prior. This single frontal film does not show a cause for the breathlessness, and the left hilar question remains unresolved.
6. Left-sided central venous catheter (F2) and prominent aortic knuckle (F4) are unchanged. Gas distension under the left dome (F3) is indeterminate for change, as the reads disagreed.
7. Multiple items are undeterminable on a single frontal view (see CAN'T DETERMINE).

RECOMMENDATIONS:
- CT chest with contrast to evaluate the left hilum (interval not specified in the findings).
- Lateral view or CT chest for the retrocardiac and left base region and for possible small nodules.
- Review source images in PACS, including bone settings and catheter windowing.
- Correlate with any previous cross-sectional imaging, the surgical history and the line insertion record.

AI DRAFT: requires resident review and attending signature.
